descriptions.title: Free real Claude via the headless CLI — the heart of the project
descriptions.body: Claude Voice's defining choice is how it reaches the genuine Claude without a per-message bill. backends.stream_claude_cli spawns `claude -p --output-format text --no-session-persistence --model sonnet`, feeds the conversation over STDIN, and runs in a neutral temp-dir cwd so no project CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded each turn. Crucially it does NOT pass --bare, because --bare would force the metered ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; instead it relies on a subscription OAuth token (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from `claude setup-token`, stored gitignored). The trade-off is latency: full agent startup costs ~20s per turn, which is fine for message surfaces but slow for live voice — so the roadmap adds a fast paid Haiku backend for conversation while keeping the free CLI for heavy work.

descriptions.title: Pluggable, toggleable brains with graceful fallback
descriptions.body: backends.py defines four streamers (ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openrouter) behind a uniform stream_reply contract that yields ('__provider__', name) then (name, chunk). enabled_chain orders the active provider first, then config 'order', among only the enabled ones. If a provider raises, stream_reply logs it and tries the next — it raises only when every enabled backend fails. This is Law 3 (degrade, never crash) made concrete: nothing about which AI answers is hardcoded; flip an 'enabled' flag in config.json to add or remove a brain.

descriptions.title: The dual-brain router — Claude vs Ronald, kept honest
descriptions.body: brain.py runs two NAMED brains: 'Claude' (engine claude_cli, the real me, voice Andrew) and 'Ronald' (engine ollama, the local stand-in, voice Brian). Ronald carries an explicit anti-hallucination system prompt — he must admit he is Ronald, has no access to Renne's calendar/projects/files, and must never invent facts. This separation was the fix for a 2026-06-21 incident where a local model impersonating Claude invented a meeting and a wrong project list. The active brain is switchable by config (default + hard-set lock) OR by name in chat ('Claude...' wakes the real me; 'Ronald, take a break' brings me back), persists in data/brain_state.json, and is shared across the PC loop, LINE, Telegram, the meeting room, and the :8720 UI. Address matching tolerates Whisper mishearings (cloud/claud/clawed...) via homophone terms plus an edit-distance-1 fuzzy fallback.

descriptions.title: Local-first, free by default
descriptions.body: Speech-to-text is always local (faster-whisper on-device), and the default brain is local Ollama on the RTX 5080 — so the assistant runs at zero marginal cost with no cloud dependency. Cloud TTS (edge-tts) degrades to offline Windows SAPI, and the GPU path degrades to CPU int8 Whisper. faster-whisper is pinned to CPU because the CUDA cublas/cuDNN DLLs are absent from this Windows Python; the LiveKit rebuild restores CUDA STT for low latency.

descriptions.title: Streaming TTS with barge-in
descriptions.body: The realtime loop (realtime.py) doesn't wait for a whole answer before speaking. speak_stream consumes the brain's token stream, flushes each complete sentence to edge-tts, and plays it via ffplay as it arrives — so Claude starts talking after the first sentence. play_interruptible watches microphone RMS during playback and terminates ffplay on sustained user speech (barge-in), cancelling the rest. Barge-in is OFF by default because, without headphones, the mic hears Claude's own voice and would cut him off; it is re-enabled with a raised RMS threshold for headphone use.

descriptions.title: Channels as adapters over one brain
descriptions.body: LINE (signed FastAPI webhook on :8721, public via Cloudflare tunnel), Telegram (outbound long-poll, no open port), and the meeting room (:8722 WebSocket) are thin adapters over the same backends + brain core. Each converts its own media to and from the common text form: inbound audio is transcoded with ffmpeg and transcribed with Whisper; outbound replies are synthesised with edge-tts (m4a for LINE, OGG/Opus for Telegram) and gated by modality.py, which decides text vs voice vs video per reply. The owner gets the full dual-brain assistant and binding controls; guests get a sandboxed social-only face.

descriptions.title: Persistence model — services, a task, and self-healing
descriptions.body: After an outage where session-launched bots died, persistence was rebuilt on Windows infrastructure. LINE, Telegram, the Cloudflare tunnel, and the brain-control API run as always-on NSSM services (QI_ClaudeVoice*), surviving reboots. The meeting room runs via a daily 08:00 scheduled task (QI_ClaudeVoiceMeeting_8AM) launched through conhost --headless wrapping a .bat (not pythonw, which crashed on null stdout) so no console window pops. An hourly task (QI_ClaudeVoiceBridgeCheck) probes the real-Claude path end to end, writes data/bridge_health.json, and alerts Renne via the Tasuke LINE notifier on failure. Configuration and small state live in JSON files — there is no database.

descriptions.title: The road to LiveKit and Voice Dispatch
descriptions.body: Research (MASTER_PLAN.md, approved 2026-06-21) selected LiveKit as the single open-source spine that satisfies natural voice AND a Zoom-like screen-share interface with one Claude agent. The mission was also re-framed: Claude Voice becomes a VOICE DISPATCH console — Renne speaks an instruction, it is classified and filed as a QI Hive dispatch (POST :9011/api/dispatch, reusing the existing CoWork queue rather than building a parallel layer), executed by headless `claude -p` + hive agents (free), and reported back by voice. Two net-new pieces are needed: a persistent dispatch executor and a notification path, since the existing apply pipeline only runs allowlisted mechanical fixes and there is no push-back today.
